questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Slovakia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Slovakia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Slovakia article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Austria in the southwest, Hungary in the south, Ukraine in the east, Poland in the north and Czech Republic in the northwest.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Slovakia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Slovakia article.

questions.proof: Its capital city is Bratislava, the only capital of the world that borders two other countries.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Slovakia about 49,034 square kilometres; North Macedonia about 25,713 square kilometres; Luxembourg about 2,593 square kilometres; Liechtenstein about 161 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bratislava?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Slovakia is Bratislava.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Slovakia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Slovakia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
